text.text: The Super A'Can was a 16-bit home video game console released by Funtech in Taiwan in 1995. Built around a Motorola 68000 processor, it featured advanced sprite hardware with scaling, rotation, and a large color palette for its time. The system used cartridge-based games and was designed to compete with the Super Nintendo and Sega Genesis, but its late release placed it against newer 32-bit consoles such as the PlayStation and Sega Saturn. With a small library of only twelve known games, the Super A'Can became one of the rarest commercial game consoles from the 1990s.
